# World Heritage Sites in the Nordic countries — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/nordic-world-heritage-sites.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/nordic-world-heritage-sites.ttl`](../decks/nordic-world-heritage-sites.ttl) · **Cards:** 44 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

All 44 UNESCO World Heritage Sites in the five Nordic countries – Sweden, Norway, Denmark (including Greenland; the Faroe Islands have none), Finland and Iceland – as inscribed on the World Heritage List on 4 October 2026, including the sites inscribed in 2025 and 2026. Front: the site, by UNESCO's English name or a short form of it and by its established Swedish name; back: the Nordic country or countries it lies in, with a note giving the year of inscription and, for sites that extend beyond the Nordic countries, the other countries. Taken from Wikidata (the English names of twelve sites are UNESCO's official names, which Wikidata does not use) and checked against UNESCO's World Heritage List, the Swedish National Heritage Board (Riksantikvarieämbetet) and the Swedish Wikipedia.

## Licensing

The content sources are Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0, and one U.S. National Park Service news release, a U.S. Government work in the public domain: the selection (every item designated a World Heritage Site in the Nordic countries), the countries, the years of inscription and of the extensions (the Moravian Church Settlements' 2024 extension from the National Park Service), the English and Swedish names that are Wikidata labels or aliases, the facts in the notes, and the Swedish place names used in the translated names come from them, so the deck can be CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. One fact in a note rests on verification sources only: for the Wadden Sea, Wikidata gives the extension years (2011 and 2014) and the three countries without qualifiers, but not that the 2014 extension was the Danish part; that is confirmed by UNESCO's secondary_dates and the Swedish Wikipedia and is stated in the compiler's own words (a fact, not expression). UNESCO's World Heritage Centre (mixed terms: CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO for © UNESCO material, but a linking policy that forbids replicating content; recorded as unknown), Riksantikvarieämbetet (CC BY 4.0) and the Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only. Twelve English fronts are UNESCO's official names of the properties in a form that is not a Wikidata label or alias (Church Town of Gammelstad, Luleå; Laponian Area; Agricultural Landscape of Southern Öland; Mining Area of the Great Copper Mountain in Falun; Grimeton Radio Station, Varberg; High Coast / Kvarken Archipelago; Rock Art of Alta; Vegaøyan – The Vega Archipelago; Jelling Mounds, Runic Stones and Church; Fortress of Suomenlinna; Verla Groundwood and Board Mill; Bronze Age Burial Site of Sammallahdenmäki); they are given as the names of things (facts, not expression), and no description, table or wording beyond those names was taken from UNESCO. Likewise one Swedish front, "Parforcejaktlandskap på norra Själland", is the title of the Swedish Wikipedia's article on the site, a name and not the article's expression; nothing else was taken from the Swedish Wikipedia; where Riksantikvarieämbetet's form of a Swedish name differs from Wikidata's, the card keeps Wikidata's. The Swedish names not in Wikidata are the compiler's own translations of UNESCO's names. The selection is the complete set of Nordic World Heritage properties, not a choice taken from any list. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence are not part of the CC0 deck: they remain under their sources' terms (Wikipedia text CC BY-SA 4.0 by Wikipedia contributors, each linked to its revision; Riksantikvarieämbetet's text CC BY 4.0; UNESCO's text under its own terms) and are short quotations given only to make the verification checkable.

## Method

1. Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with independent AI reviewers and machine checks: against live Wikidata (the builder's checks) and with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (scripts/validate_sources.ts). The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.
2. Selection from Wikidata (query 1): every item with a P1435 (heritage designation) statement whose value is World Heritage Site (Q9259) and whose P17 (country) is Sweden (Q34), Norway (Q20), Denmark (Q35), Finland (Q33), Iceland (Q189), Greenland (Q223) or the Faroe Islands (Q4628), with its P757 (World Heritage Site ID), the start time (P580) of the designation, and its English and Swedish labels. The raw CSV was saved. The query returned 66 rows: transnational sites once per Nordic country, components of sites that carry their own designation (four Hjemmeluft rock-art panels in Alta without an ID, Drottningholm Palace, its theatre, Kina slott and park with IDs 559-001…559-004, Stora Sjöfallet National Park 774-003, the Falu koppargruva item that shares ID 1027), and items that describe the same property twice (Christiansfeld, 1468, and Moravian Church Settlements, 1468bis). These were reduced to one item per World Heritage property (one property number), choosing the item that stands for the whole property: Royal Domain of Drottningholm (Q28246887), Falun och Kopparbergslagen (Q636194), Laponia (Q1137314) and Moravian Church Settlements (Q128009257). No site was found in the Faroe Islands. That gives 44 properties: 13 only in Sweden, 7 only in Norway, 10 in Denmark and 3 in Greenland, 6 only in Finland, 3 in Iceland, High Coast / Kvarken Archipelago (Sweden and Finland) and the Struve Geodetic Arc (Norway, Sweden, Finland and seven countries outside the Nordic countries).
3. Recency: the selection was checked against the 2025 (47th) and 2026 (48th) sessions of the World Heritage Committee. UNESCO's site did not answer from the research environment (every request returned a "503 Service Unavailable" page, query 2), so the Internet Archive's captures were used (queries 3–6): the World Heritage List XML export captured on 2025-07-16, the last day of the 47th session, with all 42 Nordic properties then on the List (the parse_whc.py script kept the <row> elements whose <iso_code>, split on commas, contains se, no, dk, fi, is, gl or fo, and printed id_number, date_inscribed, secondary_dates, site, states, iso_code, category, transboundary and danger), including Møns Klint, inscribed in 2025; the New Inscribed Properties page of the 48th session (2026), captured 2026-10-01, which lists two new Nordic properties, Aalto Works (Finland) and The Bony Fish Fossils of the Western Limfjord (Denmark), and boundary or criteria changes only for properties outside the Nordic countries; and the States Parties pages of Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland and Iceland captured between 2026-08-27 and 2026-09-29, after that session, whose lists of properties (read by parse_states.py from the page's links to /en/list/<number>, each number with its link text; 15, 8, 13, 8 and 3 entries, with the names UNESCO now uses) match the 44 cards exactly. UNESCO's names on those pages are the same as in the 2025 XML, so no Nordic property was renamed in 2025–2026 after Christiansfeld became part of Moravian Church Settlements (2024).
4. Labels and claims (query 7): fetch_entities.py fetched, from the Wikidata API, the English, Swedish and multilingual labels, the aliases, the Swedish and English Wikipedia sitelinks and the P757, P17 and P1435 claims (with qualifiers) of the 47 candidate items; queries 8 and 9 fetched the labels of the countries, of the Wadden Sea itself (Q26080), of the Moravian Church (Q159318) and of the places named in the translated Swedish names.
5. English names (fronts): UNESCO's official English name of each property as it stands on the States Parties pages, or a faithful short form of it where the official name has a subtitle: Kujataa ("Kujataa Greenland: Norse and Inuit Farming at the Edge of the Ice Cap"), Aasivissuit–Nipisat ("… Inuit Hunting Ground between Ice and Sea"), Vatnajökull National Park ("… – Dynamic Nature of Fire and Ice") and Bony Fish Fossils of the Western Limfjord ("The … – Evolution and Climate Adaptation in the Earliest Eocene"); for those four the short form is Wikidata's English label, except the last, whose label is the full name. Where the name on the front is also a Wikidata English label or alias, the builder checks it. Twelve fronts are UNESCO's official names in a form that is not a Wikidata label or alias (Church Town of Gammelstad, Luleå; Laponian Area; Agricultural Landscape of Southern Öland; Mining Area of the Great Copper Mountain in Falun; Grimeton Radio Station, Varberg; High Coast / Kvarken Archipelago; Rock Art of Alta; Vegaøyan – The Vega Archipelago; Jelling Mounds, Runic Stones and Church; Fortress of Suomenlinna; Verla Groundwood and Board Mill; Bronze Age Burial Site of Sammallahdenmäki); they were kept because the deck names properties as UNESCO does, and a name is a fact (see licensing). For West Norwegian Fjords – Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord the front gives only the two fjords' names (Wikidata's labels of Q193989 and Q212205, parts P527 of the property), because the full name gives the answer away; the full name is in the note.
6. Swedish names (fronts): for the 15 Swedish properties, the Wikidata Swedish label, checked against the names used by Riksantikvarieämbetet (the Swedish National Heritage Board) on its pages "Världsarv i Sverige" and "Frågor och svar om Världsarv" (query 10); 13 agree, and for two the board writes another form of the same name ("Grimeton radiostation" for Radiostationen i Grimeton, "Hälsingegårdarna" for Hälsingegårdar), see quality control. For the other countries, the Wikidata Swedish label (or multilingual label: Møns Klint, Aalto Works), checked against the Swedish Wikipedia's lists "Världsarv i Danmark", "Världsarv i Norge" and "Världsarv i Finland" and article introductions (queries 11–13; each quoted revision is linked). Where Wikidata has no Swedish name, the compiler translated UNESCO's English name into Swedish using the Swedish names of the places in it, each checked in Wikidata: Vadehavet (the Swedish label of the Wadden Sea itself, Q26080), Herrnhutarnas bosättningar (herrnhutarna, an alias of the Moravian Church, Q159318), Vikingatida ringborgar and Benfiskfossilen i västra Limfjorden (Q3801); the Swedish front of the West Norwegian Fjords is "Geirangerfjorden och Nærøyfjorden", the Swedish labels of the two fjords (Q193989, Q212205). For the par force hunting landscape the front follows the title of the Swedish Wikipedia's article, "Parforcejaktlandskap på norra Själland", rather than the Wikidata label "Parforcejaktslandskap på Norra Själland" (capital N, which Swedish does not use for "norra"). The Swedish Wikipedia's lists use equivalent Swedish names ("Ringborgar från vikingatiden", "Christiansfeld, en herrnhutnisk bosättning"). Swedish typography: between the two place names of Rjukan–Notodden and Aasivissuit–Nipisat the Swedish fronts use an en dash (tankstreck), as the English fronts and the Swedish Wikipedia's introduction of Industriminnet Rjukan–Notodden do, where the Wikidata Swedish labels have a hyphen; those two labels are therefore not checked. For Røros the Wikidata label "Bergsstaden Røros" is kept, while the Swedish Wikipedia's article is titled "Bergstaden Røros" (the Norwegian spelling); see quality control.
7. Backs: the Nordic country or countries the property lies in, from Wikidata P17, checked against UNESCO's States Parties. For the three properties in Greenland, Wikidata's P17 is Greenland and UNESCO's State Party is Denmark; the back reads "Denmark (Greenland)" / "Danmark (Grönland)". Transnational properties name every Nordic country they lie in (High Coast / Kvarken Archipelago: Sweden and Finland; Struve Geodetic Arc: Norway, Sweden and Finland, from north to south; Wadden Sea and Moravian Church Settlements: Denmark), and their notes name the other countries (Wikidata P17 and UNESCO's states).
8. Notes: the year of inscription, from the start time of Wikidata's P1435 statement, checked against UNESCO's date_inscribed (XML) or the 48th session page; extensions from Wikidata's P793 "UNESCO World Heritage Site record modification" statements with point in time P585 (Røros 2010, High Coast/Kvarken 2006, Wadden Sea 2014; Wikidata also gives 2011 for the Wadden Sea, and does not say which part was added: that the 2014 extension was the Danish part comes from UNESCO's secondary_dates and the Swedish Wikipedia, verification sources, as a fact in the compiler's words), checked against UNESCO's secondary_dates; the 2024 extension of Moravian Church Settlements, which Wikidata does not record, from the U.S. National Park Service's news release of 26 July 2024 (public domain), checked against UNESCO's secondary_dates and the XML row. A few notes add one line of context in the compiler's own words: Skogskyrkogården (a cemetery in Stockholm, Wikidata P131), Aalto Works (13 works by Alvar, Aino and Elissa Aalto: Wikidata's 13 P527 parts and their P84 architects), Þingvellir (the Swedish alias Tingvalla nationalpark) and the West Norwegian Fjords (the full official name). The builder cannot check qualifier values, so the years were compared by hand for all 44 cards (round 0).
9. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata that the item is designated a World Heritage Site (P1435 Q9259), its World Heritage Site ID (P757), each Nordic country on the back (P17) and the English and Swedish labels of those countries; the English and Swedish names on the front wherever they are Wikidata labels or aliases (the builder accepts a multilingual label for any language: Møns Klint and Aalto Works have only a mul Swedish label); and for transnational sites the other countries in the note. For translated Swedish names it checks the Swedish labels of the places named. Then the deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators.
10. Excluded: tentative-list sites and nominations not inscribed (for example the Faroe Islands' nominations), components of serial properties as cards of their own, properties whose only Nordic link is historical, and the Laponian Area's and Drottningholm's component items. Nothing in the deck depends on the World Heritage Centre's text: only facts (membership of the List, property number, States Parties, years, official names) were compared with it.

## Selection

Every property on UNESCO's World Heritage List on 4 October 2026 that lies wholly or partly in Sweden, Norway, Denmark (including Greenland; the Faroe Islands have no inscribed property), Finland or Iceland: 44 properties, each counted once, including Møns Klint (2025), Aalto Works and The Bony Fish Fossils of the Western Limfjord (both 2026). Transnational properties are one card whose back names every Nordic country they lie in, with the non-Nordic countries in the note. Left out: properties on tentative lists or nominated but not inscribed; component parts of serial properties (Wikidata gives some their own designation, e.g. Drottningholm Palace Theatre or Stora Sjöfallet National Park) as cards of their own; and Christiansfeld as a card of its own, since it has been part of the transnational property Moravian Church Settlements since 2024. The back gives the country, not the region or municipality; for Greenland it gives Denmark, the State Party, with Greenland in brackets.

## Queries

**1. Every item designated a World Heritage Site (P1435 Q9259) whose country (P17) is a Nordic country, with its ID (P757), the designation's start/end time and labels (saved as q1.rq; curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q1.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql -o q1.csv)** (Wikidata: items with the heritage designation (P1435) World Heritage Site (Q9259) in the Nordic countries, their World Heritage Site IDs (P757), countries (P17), start times and English, Swedish and multilingual labels)

```
SELECT ?site ?siteEn ?siteSv ?whsId ?rank ?start ?end ?country ?countryEn WHERE {
  VALUES ?country { wd:Q34 wd:Q20 wd:Q35 wd:Q33 wd:Q189 wd:Q223 wd:Q4628 }
  ?site p:P1435 ?st .
  ?st ps:P1435 wd:Q9259 ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
  ?site wdt:P17 ?country .
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P580 ?start }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P582 ?end }
  OPTIONAL { ?site wdt:P757 ?whsId }
  OPTIONAL { ?site rdfs:label ?siteEn FILTER(LANG(?siteEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?site rdfs:label ?siteSv FILTER(LANG(?siteSv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countryEn FILTER(LANG(?countryEn) = "en") }
}
ORDER BY ?countryEn ?whsId
```

**2. Attempts to fetch UNESCO's list directly (each returned UNESCO's "503 Service Unavailable" page, 21126 bytes)** (UNESCO World Heritage Centre: the World Heritage List (XML export), the States Parties pages of Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland and Iceland, and New Inscribed Properties (48COM, 2026))

```
curl -s -L --max-time 120 -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o whc-list.xml -w "%{http_code} %{size_download}\n" "https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/xml/"
curl -s -L --max-time 120 -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o whc-se.html -w "%{http_code} %{size_download}\n" "https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/se"
curl -s -L --max-time 120 -A "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/130.0 Safari/537.36 (solid-memo deck research; https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o whc-se.html -w "%{http_code} %{size_download}\n" "https://whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/se"
curl -s -L --max-time 60 -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{size_download}\n" "https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1752"
```

## Quality control

5 rounds, 31 findings: 23 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 8 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (350 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's site, country and year against Wikidata and UNESCO's World Heritage List (2025 XML export, 2026 States Parties pages and the 48th session's new inscriptions); the Swedish names against Riksantikvarieämbetet and the Swedish Wikipedia. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 44 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.

Wikidata and UNESCO agree on the membership of the List, the property numbers, the Nordic countries and the year of inscription of all 44 properties; no card follows a value that a better source contradicts, and no Wikidata check was skipped because it failed. The discrepancies are in Wikidata's modelling (components and duplicate items with World Heritage designations, two start times for Røros, a missing Swedish label on some newer items), in two Swedish-name forms where Riksantikvarieämbetet and Wikidata differ, and in two years in the Swedish Wikipedia's tables; they were resolved as below. The year of inscription cannot be checked by the builder (it is a qualifier) and was compared by hand for every card.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| royal-domain-of-drottningholm | Wikidata gives the World Heritage designation and ID 559 both to the property item (Q28246887, Royal Domain of Drottningholm) and to the palace item (Q208559, also ID 559-001), and separate IDs to the theatre, Kina slott and the park. | One card for the property, using Q28246887 (whose labels are UNESCO's and Riksantikvarieämbetet's names); components left out. | fixed |
| great-copper-mountain-in-falun | Two Wikidata items carry ID 1027: Falun och Kopparbergslagen (Q636194, start time 2001) and Falu koppargruva (Q15107508, no start time), the mine itself. | Card uses Q636194, whose Swedish label is the name Riksantikvarieämbetet uses ("Falun och Kopparbergslagen"); the English front is UNESCO's name, not a Wikidata label, so it is not checked. | fixed |
| moravian-church-settlements | Wikidata has Christiansfeld (Q3197288, ID 1468, inscribed 2015) and Moravian Church Settlements (Q128009257, ID 1468bis). UNESCO lists one property, 1468, "Moravian Church Settlements" (Denmark, Germany, United Kingdom, United States), first inscribed in 2015 and extended in 2024. | One card under the present name; back Denmark; the note gives Christiansfeld, 2015, and the 2024 extension with the other countries. Christiansfeld is not a card of its own. | fixed |
| roros-mining-town | Wikidata's P1435 statement has two start times, 1980 and 1985 (year precision); UNESCO gives date_inscribed 1980 and secondary_dates 2010 (the extension to the Circumference). The Swedish Wikipedia list also gives 1980. | Note: inscribed 1980, extended 2010. The 1985 value in Wikidata is not used. | fixed |
| sammallahdenmaki | The Swedish Wikipedia's table "Världsarv i Finland" gives 1996; UNESCO (date_inscribed 1999) and Wikidata (start time 1999) give 1999. | Note 1999 (UNESCO and Wikidata). | no change needed |
| agricultural-landscape-of-southern-oland | The Swedish Wikipedia's table "Världsarv i Sverige" gives 2001; UNESCO, Wikidata and Riksantikvarieämbetet give 2000. | Note 2000. | no change needed |
| grimeton-radio-station | Riksantikvarieämbetet writes "Grimeton radiostation"; Wikidata's Swedish label and the Swedish Wikipedia write "Radiostationen i Grimeton". | Kept the Wikidata form (the CC0 content source; Riksantikvarieämbetet is a verification source); both forms are in the evidence. | no change needed |
| decorated-farmhouses-of-halsingland | Riksantikvarieämbetet writes "Hälsingegårdarna" (definite form); Wikidata's Swedish label and the Swedish Wikipedia ("Världsarvet Hälsingegårdar") write "Hälsingegårdar". | Kept "Hälsingegårdar" (Wikidata); the evidence records both. | no change needed |
| church-town-of-gammelstad | Riksantikvarieämbetet's FAQ list writes "Gammelstad kyrkstad", its list of sites "Gammelstads kyrkstad", as do Wikidata and the Swedish Wikipedia. | "Gammelstads kyrkstad". | no change needed |
| par-force-hunting-landscape | Wikidata's Swedish label is "Parforcejaktslandskap på Norra Själland", with a capital N that Swedish does not use for "norra"; the Swedish Wikipedia article is titled "Parforcejaktlandskap på norra Själland" and begins "Parforcejaktlandskapet på norra Själland är ett av Danmarks världsarv". | Swedish front "Parforcejaktlandskapet på norra Själland"; no check on the Swedish label of the site (it would fail on the capital letter), the Swedish label of Själland (Q25535) is checked instead. | fixed |

Its start time is 2009, the year of the first inscription (Germany and the Netherlands); the Danish part was added in 2014 (UNESCO secondary_dates 2014; the Swedish Wikipedia). | Swedish name "Vadehavet", the Swedish label of the Wadden Sea itself (Q26080), checked; the note gives 2009 and the Danish part in 2014, and Germany and the Netherlands (P17 checked). Wikidata (Q64590476) gives the extension years 2011 and 2014 (P793/P585) and P17 Denmark, Germany and the Netherlands without qualifiers; it does not say that the Danish part was added in 2014, which rests on UNESCO's secondary_dates and the Swedish Wikipedia (verification sources, a fact stated in the compiler's words). | fixed |

| bony-fish-fossils-of-the-western-limfjord | Inscribed in July 2026; Wikidata's English label is UNESCO's full name and there is no Swedish label or Swedish Wikipedia article. ### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 44 cards: membership of the List, countries, years of inscription and extensions, transnational notes and Swedish names, against the reviewer's own Wikidata query, the builder's live checks, the 2025 and 2026 sessions and national sources.

No factual errors; all 44 cards correct as of 2026-10-04 and the round-0 fixes confirmed. Two suggestions, both applied: the Aalto Works note now names Alvar, Aino and Elissa Aalto, and the West Norwegian Fjords front no longer contains the answer.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| aalto-works | The note "Buildings by Alvar Aalto and his studio" is narrower than the property as inscribed, which UNESCO and the Finnish government describe as the shared work of Alvar, Aino and Elissa Aalto and their studio. | Verified: UNESCO's 48COM entry names Alvar Aalto, Aino Marsio-Aalto, Elissa Aalto and the Aalto studio, and the Swedish Wikipedia says the 13 objects were designed by Alvar Aalto with Aino and Elissa Aalto. Note changed to "13 works of architecture by Alvar, Aino and Elissa Aalto. Inscribed 2026." / "13 arkitekturverk av Alvar, Aino och Elissa Aalto. Världsarv sedan 2026.", supported by Wikidata (13 P527 parts, P84 architects Alvar, Aino and Elissa Aalto) with new checks (the builder reads only best-rank values, so Elissa Aalto, a normal-rank architect of Muuratsalo Experimental House beside Alvar Aalto at preferred rank, is in the evidence but not checked); "studio" left out because no content source states it (see round 3). | fixed |
| west-norwegian-fjords | The front "West Norwegian Fjords – Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord" / "Västnorska fjordar – …" gives the answer (Norway) away. | Agreed. Front changed to the two fjords, "Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord" / "Geirangerfjorden och Nærøyfjorden" (Wikidata labels of Q193989 and Q212205, both P527 parts of the property, checked); UNESCO's full name moved to the note. The weaker place hints in Church Town of Gammelstad, Luleå and Grimeton Radio Station, Varberg name towns, not the country, and are kept as part of UNESCO's names. | fixed |

### Round 2: Language, translation and language tags (2026-10-04)

Tags, Swedish names and conventions found in order and the round-0 language fixes confirmed. One warning (an undocumented spelling difference for Røros) is now documented; of three suggestions, the en dash and the Tingvalla note were applied and the Møns Klint / Stevns klint capitalisation was kept with a reason.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
